title: The Sub-Menu That Tastes of Older Software

features.name: nested-menus
features.desc-on-touch: Menus folding into menus: the 1987 version showing the 1995 version showing the 2004 version. All three still executing, nested inside each other like a Russian doll of amber text.

features.name: amber-terminal-stack
features.desc-on-touch: An old monitor inside an older monitor inside an even older monitor. Each screen shows what the next one was before it was born. The phosphor hums.

features.name: menu-dwelling
features.desc-on-touch: A small house built from menu syntax. Every doorway is labeled with F-key combinations that haven't worked since 1994. The walls taste of plastic.

features.name: cascading-error
features.desc-on-touch: An error message that spawns smaller error messages inside itself, each quoting the one above it. The innermost one is a typo. It has always been a typo.

inscription: every submenu carries the ghost of the software version that created it; the code remembers itself deeper than the machine does

file.name: MenuSystem_Bootstrap_v0.7_FINAL.log
file.note: The first menu ever compiled on this terminal. It is still receiving input and generating responses. No one knows how.

exits.label: back to the menu containing this menu
into a version where the text reads backward and forward at the same time
deeper into code that predates human symbol-making
